facts.text: Lexington was originally called Greenbush before 1842 when Reuben Dimond renamed it to honor his wife's ancestor Ethan Allen, echoing Lexington, Massachusetts.
The Cadillac House, built in the 1840s, welcomed lumber barons, sailors, and stagecoach passengers and still operates as an inn today.
Lexington became the first county seat of Sanilac County in 1848, holding that title until 1879 when the seat moved to Sandusky.
A 1913 storm destroyed major docks, shifting the village’s economy from lumber and shipping to farming, fishing, and tourism.
The village’s harbor received major improvements in 1965 under the River and Harbor Act, boosting recreational boating and solidifying Lexington’s role as a boating hub.
Lexington’s downtown features brick commercial buildings that once housed a bank, a library, and shops, reflecting its 19th‑century prosperity.
